name: SaaS Starter Stack
tagline: Next.js SaaS with auth, billing, and teams wired up
description: The fastest path from idea to first paying customer. Next.js 16, Auth.js sessions, Stripe subscriptions with teams, Postgres schema migrations, and a component library — all documented as a starter concept.
features: Auth.js with magic link, OAuth, and session rotation
Stripe subscriptions, trials, and seat-based billing
Team accounts with roles and invites
CI pipeline: lint, typecheck, test, preview deploys
includes: Component-library concept covering common interface primitives

faqs.a: Next.js 16, TypeScript, Tailwind, Postgres (Prisma), Auth.js, Stripe, and Vercel-ready out of the box.

faqs.q: Can I use it for a client project?
faqs.a: Yes with the Extended License, including white-labeling.
The setup guide outlines a path from configuration to a running preview.

name: AI App Scaffold
tagline: LLM app boilerplate: RAG, streaming, and evals
description: A production scaffold for LLM apps: streaming chat UI, retrieval-augmented generation with pgvector, tool-calling patterns, token accounting, and an eval harness with 30 golden cases.
features: Streaming chat UI with markdown and code rendering
RAG pipeline with pgvector and hybrid search

faqs.a: OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google via a provider-agnostic adapter; swap with one env var.

faqs.q: Is RAG included or a stub?
faqs.a: Fully implemented: ingestion, chunking, hybrid search, reranking, and citation rendering.

faqs.q: Can I ship it as a product?
faqs.a: Yes — Extended License covers commercial products.

name: Chrome Extension Forge
tagline: MV3 extension starter with options page and sync
description: Forge your next extension fast: Manifest V3, content scripts, options page with sync storage, service worker patterns, and a build pipeline that passes the Web Store review first try.
features: Manifest V3 with declarative net request examples
Content script injection with isolated-world helpers
Web Store submission checklist and screenshots pack

faqs.a: The same source builds for Firefox with a config flag; both manifests ship.
Recommended (esbuild), but the src/ runs unpacked with no build for quick experiments.
Includes Stripe Checkout wiring examples for premium features.

name: Serverless API Kit
tagline: Edge functions, auth, and rate limits — pre-wired
description: A serverless API foundation on edge runtimes: JWT auth, rate limiting, validation with Zod, observability hooks, and a test suite that runs in seconds.
includes: Full source with two runtime adapters

faqs.q: Can I use it with Supabase?
faqs.a: Yes — an adapter swaps the auth layer to Supabase JWTs in one file.

faqs.q: Is it for REST or GraphQL?
faqs.a: REST out of the box; a GraphQLYoga adapter is in the extras folder.
The edge handlers start in under 5ms on major providers; benchmarks included.

name: Mobile Flutter Launchpad
tagline: Cross-platform app starter with auth and themes
description: A Flutter launchpad with clean architecture: feature-first folders, Riverpod state, theming, deep linking, and CI that builds both stores' artifacts.
features: Deep linking and push notification setup
CI: lint, test, and store artifact builds

faqs.q: iOS and Android from one codebase?
faqs.a: Yes — the CI builds both, plus a macOS flavor as a bonus.
A Supabase integration layer ships wired and ready.
Fully null-safe on stable Dart 3.x.

name: Design System Blueprint
tagline: Tokens, components, and docs — the whole machine
description: A design system skeleton: semantic tokens, a11y-tested primitives, Storybook docs, and a Figma library that mirrors the code. Extend it instead of reinventing it.
features: Component-library concept spanning common primitives such as buttons and dialogs
Storybook docs with controls and play functions
Figma library mapped to token names

faqs.a: Primitives are framework-neutral CSS + vanilla JS; React wrappers are included as an example.
Tokens sync via Tokens Studio; the mapping guide is in the docs.
Primitives target AA contrast by default; axe tests run in CI.

name: E-Commerce Engine
tagline: Storefront starter with cart, checkout, and taxes
description: A storefront engine with product catalog, cart, Stripe checkout, tax estimation, and order management. SEO-baked: JSON-LD, sitemaps, and image optimization out of the box.
features: Catalog with variants, inventory, and search
Cart with persistent state and guest checkout
SEO layer: JSON-LD, sitemap, OG tags

faqs.a: Yes — fulfillment switches to instant download links, perfect for this very store pattern.
Headless-ready: a storefront API mode powers any front end.
Stripe cards, Apple/Google Pay, and Link by default.

name: CLI Toolkit Foundation
description: A CLI foundation with command registration, config files, spinners, prompts, update checks, and a plugin API. Ships with packaging for npm and Homebrew.
features: Packaging: npm, Homebrew tap, standalone binary

faqs.a: The core is Node; the patterns port to Go/Python — a porting guide is included.
That's exactly what it's for — several buyers wrap internal DevOps tools with it.
Snapshot tests for CLI output and a golden-command suite.
